column1: # Golden deletion vectors written by Apache Iceberg Java 1.10.0.
# Every *.bin file except legacy32_runs is the deletion-vector-v1 blob that
# BitmapPositionDeleteIndex.serialize() returns: the 4-byte length, magic, 64-bit
# portable roaring bitmap and CRC-32, exactly as Iceberg writes it into a Puffin
# file. legacy32_runs is an unframed 32-bit portable bitmap, the legacy format
# the reader still accepts. Iceberg Java run-encodes containers when that is
# smaller, which DeletionVectorWriter never does, so these files also cover run
# containers written by another engine.
# Each record: <name> TAB <blob SHA-256> TAB <cardinality> TAB <first position>
#   TAB <last position> TAB <SHA-256 of the positions as little-endian int64>
# The last four columns are what Iceberg Java decodes from the blob
# (PositionDeleteIndex.deserialize + forEach). The blob SHA-256 guards against
# the fixtures changing; regenerate them only from Iceberg Java, never by hand.
# Cases:
#   single                   one array container holding one position
#   sparse_random            1000 random draws below 1M: sixteen array containers
#   dense_random             about half of the first 200000 rows: bitset containers plus a run container
#   every_other              every even row below 131072: two bitset containers that never run-encode
#   ranges                   contiguous ranges, including one that crosses a container boundary: run containers
#   mixed_containers         array, run and bitset containers in one group
#   array_bitset_threshold   4096 values (largest array container) next to 4097 (smallest bitset container)
#   container_boundaries     positions at 0, 65535/65536, 2^31-1/2^31 and 2^32-1
#   multi_group              groups 0, 1 and 7; Iceberg Java also writes the empty groups in between
#   high_group               group 0 and group 100, including the last position of group 100
#   full_container           all 65536 rows of one container: a single run
#   legacy32_runs            unframed 32-bit portable bitmap written by RoaringBitmap 1.3.0, with runs

sparse_random
